findings.finding: The entire hero idea (I1, the hard case) and the sustainability claim are built on the premise that ASIN B0HC6CLNFS currently ships in 'a plain single-use poly bag' with loose pins. No scout fact_id supports this for this ASIN — scout never even lists current packaging as a gap, let alone a fact. The only sources in play are (a) buyer's own conditional, hypothetical fear ('If it's loose pins rattling in a flimsy poly bag...') and (b) scout's description of a rival's tile (Genuine Innovations, F4-adjacent, 'shown beside a flat sheet of rubber plug strips'), not this listing. Innovaty converts a buyer hypothetical + a competitor's packaging into an assumed fact about this product ('the poly bag as sole packaging layer', 'replacing the poly bag'), and genius's BOM inherits it verbatim ('Hinged hard case ... replacing the poly bag [I1]'). The sustainability claim ('reduces poly-bag film per unit versus the prior poly-bag packaging') then makes a quantitative comparison against an unverified baseline — exactly the kind of claim Amazon's content review flags (genius's own premortem #5).
findings.fix: Scout should add 'current retail packaging/box format for B0HC6CLNFS' as an explicit gap or, budget permitting, source it. Until then, innovaty should reword every instance ('current packaging is believed/assumed to be a poly bag, unconfirmed') and genius should either soften the sustainability claim to a forward-looking commitment ('our new packaging uses X% less single-use film than a standard poly-bag baseline for this category') rather than a claim about 'the prior' packaging of this specific ASIN.

findings.finding: This field describes a 'second foil-sealed sub-pack of 5 spare bacon strips (10 strips total in the box) plus one spare deflating pin, nested in a dedicated extra slot in the hard case' with no idea_id tag and no version note. This directly conflicts with the now-reconciled v1_hero_case scope: (1) 'foil-sealed' is I2's mechanism, which innovaty's own version_plan defers to v2_later; (2) it contradicts innovaty's own listing_implications.image_briefs_2_to_4[1], which describes 'five rubber strips each in a labeled slot exactly as they ship today' for the hero-case image; (3) genius's costed v1_hero_case BOM has qty:5 for the rubber strips and no line item at all for a spare pin or a second foil pouch — so this feature is both uncosted and untooled if it ships in v1. This is exactly the kind of leftover the orchestrator's I1-only reconciliation pass should have caught but the packaging/color_strategy fields did and this one didn't.
findings.fix: Either (a) delete bundle_or_addition from the v1 plan and explicitly fold it into the I2/I3/I4 v2_later fast-follow with its own cost line for genius to price, or (b) if it's meant to ship at launch, tag it with an idea_id, add it to genius's v1_hero_case BOM (extra pin + extra strip-slot foam cut + a second pouch), and reconcile the strip count everywhere (image briefs, image prompts, sustainability BOM comparison).

findings.finding: what_i_cut states the multi-language paper booklet is 'replaced for v1 by numbered pins and the hard case's own slotted organization.' But the numbered pins are idea I5, and innovaty's own version_plan.v2_later explicitly defers I5 ('Next scheduled mold revision... gated on a quick freedom-to-operate check', medium prior_art_risk). So the reconciled v1_hero_case actually ships with: no booklet (cut), no numbered pins (deferred to v2), and no QR card (I3, also deferred). That leaves zero in-box instructional aid for a first-time buyer at launch — a direct conflict with the knowledge base's own playbook item ('instructions unclear → the first attempt succeeds unread') and with buyer's fear #5 (pin/threading sequence confusion, marked 'answered_by: bullet', which itself is thin).
findings.fix: Rewrite what_i_cut to state accurately that v1 has no numbered pins yet, and either (a) add a minimal, near-zero-cost printed step card to v1_hero_case scope (cheaper than I3's QR version) so first-use isn't unread-and-unguided, or (b) explicitly accept the risk and have genius price a bullet-only mitigation with no visual aid, flagged in the premortem.

findings.finding: Genius's BOM line for the aluminum tool body cites '~48g per F3' as the tool body's own weight. But scout's F3 actually says the whole kit 'ship[s] with 3 plug tools and 5 vulcanized-rubber sealing strips, and weigh[s] about 48 grams' — i.e. 48g is the total shipped-kit weight (tool + strips), not the metal body alone. Genius's unit_weight_g (93g for v1_hero_case) appears to add the case and other parts on top of a tool-body figure that already includes the strips, double-counting or overstating the base product's weight contribution. This is a classic 'numbers pulled from a different shape of the product' mix-up, and it feeds directly into premortem #3 (packaged dimensions/weight crossing the FBA size-tier line), which genius uses to justify widening the fba_fee_usd high bound.
findings.fix: Re-derive unit_weight_g from scout's F3 as: tool body + pins ≈ a fraction of 48g (strips are a small fraction of that total), not 48g for the tool alone. Get an actual supplier weight for the tool body before locking case/foam dimensions, since this number is load-bearing for the size-tier risk genius itself flags.

findings.finding: weeks_to_first_sale is 24.3 / 31.05 / 37.8 — only about ±21.7% around base, narrower than the ±30% floor the brief calls for on uncertain estimates. Several individual phases are narrower still (phase 2 'prototypes/fit-test/compliance' ≈±20.6%, phase 3 'soft tooling/T1' ≈±20%, phase 5 'production run' ≈±14%, phase 6 'freight/FBA check-in' ≈±16.7%) because the multiplier was applied uniformly to the knowledge base's own narrow per-phase ranges without widening for this specific launch's flagged risks: a 22%-probability 'fatal' tariff/HTS premortem item, a medium prior-art item, and first-time compliance testing (Prop 65, shake-drop, accelerated aging) that has no track record with this supplier pair.
findings.fix: Widen phases 2, 3, 5 and 6 to at least ±30% around their base, particularly the tooling and compliance-testing phases, given the tariff/HTS uncertainty genius itself rates as a fatal-impact premortem risk.

findings.finding: N3 ('I need proof — real ride reports... that a plug holds for actual mileage') is the single highest-severity need in the whole file (severity 8) and is the direct justification for idea I3 (the QR proof card), yet unlike N1/N2 it carries no evidence_cluster_ids and cites no scout fact_id — it is buyer's own unsourced inference from the general absence of reviews (which is really F11, the blocked-fetch gap, not a complaint cluster). N4 (severity 5, 'need to know one kit covers both road and MTB tires') is similarly uncited, even though scout's own unanswered_questions list already names this exact gap and could have been cited.
findings.fix: Add evidence_cluster_ids or an explicit fact_id reference (F11 for N3's 'no proof/no reviews' framing; the relevant unanswered_questions entry for N4) so both needs trace to a source per the 'sources or silence' rule, especially since N3 alone drives a costed idea (I3, ~$800 one-off).

findings.finding: Claims the tile needs to 'separate... from the white-background, silver-tool rivals in the same grid row,' but no scout fact_id describes any competitor's image background — scout's competitor entries (Genuine Innovations, Stan's Dart, Dynaplug) describe tool shape only, never background color. Separately, because I4 (the only change to the tool's own finish, which buyer explicitly said would read as 'authority... not a toy') is correctly deferred to v2, the v1 hero image differentiates using only the case and a background gradient, while the tool itself stays the same silver/raw finish buyer's own three_second_scan rated 'neutral' (not 'pull'), unlike Dynaplug's housing. The plan should be honest that v1's thumbnail lift rests entirely on the case, not on the tool finish buyer actually reacted to.
findings.fix: Either cite a real source for rival background colors or soften the claim to a design choice rather than a competitive-differentiation fact; and add a line acknowledging that v1's click-through gain depends solely on the case shape being visible at 300px, since the tool finish itself remains a 'neutral' signal until I4 ships.

findings.finding: errc.raise cites 'foil seal + pack date' (I2) and errc.create cites the 'QR-linked bench-test video + printed proof card' (I3) as part of the product's differentiation, with no note that both are v2_later fast-follow items, not part of the v1_hero_case launch being recommended. Every other innovaty field that touches I2/I3/I4 (packaging, color_strategy, what_i_cut, image_prompts) is careful to flag the version split; the ERRC summary is the one place that isn't, and a reader skimming only ERRC would think these ship at launch.
findings.fix: Add a 'ships v2' parenthetical to the raise/create bullets that reference I2/I3, matching the labeling discipline used elsewhere in the file.

findings.finding: Invokes a 'costly signal' argument ('visible spare capacity is a costly signal that partly offsets not having reviews yet') without the formal sutherland.costly_signal tag that the adjacent packaging.upgrade_vs_category field correctly uses inline for the same concept. Untagged judgements score at half weight.
findings.fix: Add the explicit tag, or fold this reasoning into the already-tagged packaging.upgrade_vs_category field once K2 is resolved.

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: The plan's whole hero fix rests on an unconfirmed premise: nobody actually verified that this ASIN currently ships in a poly bag. That's inferred from the buyer persona's hypothetical fear and a rival's product photo, not from anything scout observed about B0HC6CLNFS itself — and it's also the basis for a sustainability comparison claim that Amazon's content review is specifically likely to challenge.

Two pieces of the plan still describe features genius explicitly deferred to a later, uncosted v2 (a 10-strip/spare-pin bundle using I2's foil-seal mechanism, and a claim that numbered pins replace the instruction booklet). If shipped as written, day-one units have no install instructions at all — no booklet, no QR card, no numbered pins — and an uncosted extra part in the case.

A 48-gram figure that scout sourced for the entire kit (tool plus 5 strips) got relabeled in the cost model as the weight of the metal tool alone, inflating the unit weight used to judge whether the new hard case stays under the FBA size-tier line — worth a real supplier weight before locking case dimensions, since that exact risk is already flagged as a premortem item.
